metaTitle: Best Leaf Blowers for Gutters in 2026
metaDescription: Five cordless pole blowers that clear gutters from the ground, compared by reach, weight, airflow and battery so you can skip the ladder.
expertTake: The Seesii 700 CFM pole kit is the best gutter blower because it pairs the highest airflow with two 4.0Ah batteries and a handheld mode for the rest of the yard. The ADOTOCAM is the value pick for anyone already on DeWalt 20V MAX batteries. Skip pole blowers if your gutters are packed with wet, rotted debris or your house is more than two stories, because a blower only clears loose material.
introParagraphs: Clearing gutters from the ground means a blower with a long, angled tube that reaches the trough while you stand on the lawn. Air lifts and flushes dry or lightly damp leaves out of the channel, which saves a risky ladder climb and a bucket of slimy debris.

The limits are physics. A tube held at arm's length multiplies the weight of the motor, and a blower that feels light in the hand feels heavy at the end of eight feet of pole. Reach, weight and a good angled head matter more than headline air speed.

products.name: Seesii 700 CFM cordless pole blower, 200 MPH, 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The Seesii is a two-in-one: bolt on the extension to reach a gutter, or remove it and use the tool as a handheld blower for patios and drives. A high-torque motor produces 700 CFM, the most airflow of any pole blower in this guide, and three speed modes let you start gently so the first blast does not spray debris straight back at you.

The two 4.0Ah batteries are the quiet advantage. Gutter work is slow, with pauses to reposition and check progress, and a second pack means you can finish a house without stopping to charge. Against the Alloyman, which moves 580 CFM from a similar layout, the Seesii has roughly 20 percent more air, which matters on packed, damp leaf mats.

Expect the reach to be about 8.9 feet in total, so it suits a single-story eave or the low edge of a two-story roof. Check the pole joints before each job, wipe leaf slime off the tube so it does not cake and flake into the motor, and store the batteries at partial charge. Gutters are best cleared on a dry day, because dry oak and maple leaves lift in a single pass while the same leaves after rain become a sticky mat that no 700 CFM jet will fully shift.
products.bestFor: Owners of single-story homes who want the most airflow and a second battery.
pros: 700 CFM is the top pole-blower airflow here
cons: Reach is about 8.9 ft, short for tall eaves

products.name: Alloyman 40V brushless gutter blower, 55 inch pole, 580 CFM
products.description:
Alloyman builds its pitch around reach: a pole that extends to 55 inches, which is the adjustable length that brings the nozzle to the gutter on a one or two story house. A rotating angled head lets you aim into corners, tight eaves or ground piles without repositioning, and the brushless 40V motor produces 580 CFM at 180 MPH.

Adjustability is the selling point. A fixed-length pole forces you to hold a blower at an awkward height, while an extendable one lets you hold the tool close to your body for the first reach and extend it as you need. The trade-off against the Seesii is less airflow, 580 against 700 CFM, and no spare battery information on the listing.

Gutter work is dirty. Wipe the pole and the head after each job so wet leaf residue does not harden, check the pole lock for slippage before you extend it over your head, and keep goggles on to guard against flying debris. Work from the downspout end away from it, so loose material is pushed toward open trough rather than packed into the outlet where it forms a plug.
products.bestFor: Two-story homes where adjustable reach matters more than the last bit of airflow.
cons: Battery details are not clear on the listing
Locking mechanism needs checking before use

products.name: Feihu 40V brushless pole blower, 580 CFM, 300 degree tube
products.description:
Feihu is the one to look at for aim. A tube that rotates 300 degrees lets you angle the nozzle along the trough from almost any standing position, and a metal extension rod resists the flex that cheaper plastic poles show when you lift them overhead. It uses the same 580 CFM and 180 MPH figures as the Alloyman, from a 40V brushless motor.

The batteries are small. Two 2.0Ah packs are among the lowest capacities in this guide, so expect shorter running time than the Seesii's 4.0Ah pair. For a quick pass over one gutter it is enough; for a whole house you will recharge between sections.

After a job, rinse leaf residue off the rod, dry the joints, and put the packs on the charger indoors. Metal rods are stiffer but heavier, so test the balance with the battery in place before you buy for a long reach. Because the head swivels, work with the nozzle pointed slightly downward along the trough, which keeps debris traveling away from your face and off the shingles.
products.bestFor: Gutters with awkward corners where tube angle matters most.
cons: Only 2.0Ah per battery, so runtime is short
Metal rod adds weight at the end of a lever

products.name: iToolMax 7.8 ft gutter blower, 400W, 5.5 lb, 2 x 3.0Ah
products.description:
iToolMax is the light one: 5.5 pounds in a package with a 7.8 foot reach, which is easiest on the wrists and shoulders because the weight at the end of a pole is what tires you out. The 400W motor spins at 29,000 rpm for 520 CFM and 150 MPH, a gentler jet than the 700 CFM Seesii.

That gentler profile is a feature for dry leaves and a limit on wet ones. A 150 MPH jet will not blast compacted, soaked debris out of a gutter, so pair it with a scoop for the first pass if your gutters are packed. It is a good fit for an older homeowner or anyone who wants to limit fatigue.

Two 3.0Ah packs sit between the Feihu's 2.0Ah and the Seesii's 4.0Ah. Store the packs indoors, and look over the pole joints for cracks, since plastic fatigues at the joint where you flex the tool overhead. A short test lift in the yard, holding the pole at full height for thirty seconds, tells you whether you can sustain the weight for a whole eave.
products.bestFor: Users who prioritise low weight and easy handling for dry leaves.
pros: Only 5.5 pounds, easy to hold up
7.8 ft reach covers a one-story eave
Gentle jet is easy to control
cons: 150 MPH struggles with wet compacted debris

products.name: ADOTOCAM 20V pole blower for DeWalt batteries, 580 CFM, tool only
products.description:
ADOTOCAM is a clever use of an existing battery platform: it runs on DeWalt 20V MAX packs you may already own, which skips the highest cost in a cordless tool. The brushless motor spins at 26,000 rpm for 580 CFM and 180 MPH, and the tool switches between an extended pole and a compact handheld in seconds.

The catch is that it is a tool-only purchase. You must supply the batteries, and a compatibility issue with a different pack generation would be your problem to solve. This is also an aftermarket adapter-style tool, not an official DeWalt product, so check warranty terms carefully before relying on it.

If you do own DeWalt packs, this is a very low-cost way to get a gutter blower. Keep the pack seat clean and dry, and check that the battery latches firmly before you hold the tool overhead. A loose pack on a pole above your head is the one failure mode that can drop hardware on you, so seat it firmly and tug it before every lift.
products.bestFor: Owners of DeWalt 20V MAX batteries who want a gutter tool without buying more packs.
pros: Runs on existing DeWalt 20V MAX packs
Quick switch between pole and handheld
Lowest total cost for DeWalt owners
cons: Fit with newer pack generations must be checked

buyingCriteria.explanation: A pole multiplies the weight of the blower at your hands, so a 5.5 pound tool like the iToolMax feels far lighter than a heavier one at the same reach. The Alloyman's 55 inch pole is adjustable, while the Seesii reaches about 8.9 feet. For a single-story eave, 8 feet is enough; for two stories, pick the longer adjustable option and expect a workout.

A good angled head lets you point the jet along the trough rather than straight into it. The Feihu's 300 degree tube and the Alloyman's rotating head both help. A fixed straight tube will blow debris back onto the roof or at your face.

Wet debris needs speed to break its grip, while dry leaves need volume. The Seesii's 700 CFM and 200 MPH covers both, while the iToolMax's 150 MPH is gentler. If your gutters are packed with rotted material, no blower will fully clear them.
Gutter work is slow, so runtime matters more than turbo. The Seesii's two 4.0Ah packs outlast the Feihu's two 2.0Ah packs. A cordless blower with 2.0Ah may need a charging break to finish a house.
The ADOTOCAM is sold tool only, so you must own DeWalt 20V MAX packs. A kit like the Seesii includes batteries and a charger. Compare the total cost of the working setup, not only the tool.

A blower clears loose, dry or lightly damp leaves. It will not unclog a full downspout or lift packed wet muck. Plan to follow with a hose or scoop if the gutters are heavily compacted, and treat a blower as a yearly tidy-up tool that works best when it is used before debris has had a wet winter to rot down into sludge.

howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated pole length and tool weight together, from the iToolMax's 5.5 lb and 7.8 ft to the Alloyman's 55 inch adjustable pole. A long pole on a heavy tool tires the user fast.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared CFM and MPH from the Seesii's 700 and 200 down to the iToolMax's 520 and 150. Gutters need both volume and speed for wet debris.

howWeEvaluated.title: Aim and head design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each tool angles its jet, from the Feihu's 300 degree tube to simple fixed designs. Aim decides whether debris leaves the gutter.

cards.label: Pole blower
cards.text: The Seesii, Alloyman and Feihu are built for reaching up. They save a ladder climb but tire your arms. They suit owners who clear gutters each autumn and want one tool to do it.

cards.label: Handheld blower
cards.text: A standard handheld cannot reach the gutter, but it is lighter. A pole blower that converts, like the Seesii or ADOTOCAM, gives you both. Choose a convertible if you also want a yard blower.

howToChoose.note: Choose a convertible pole blower if you want one tool for gutters and the yard.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High speed and volume, and a plan for a scoop on the first pass. Wet leaves compact into a mat that a blower alone will not lift. Start at a low setting so the jet does not splash debris at you.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Seesii at 700 CFM and 200 MPH is the strongest, and the Alloyman at 580 CFM is the best reach. The iToolMax at 150 MPH is better for dry leaves.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a two-story house or a lot of overhanging trees. The Seesii's two 4.0Ah packs and the Alloyman's adjustable reach are worth the extra cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have one story and a few trees. The iToolMax or ADOTOCAM does the job at a low tier.

maintenance.why: Wet leaf residue dries into crust that jams joints. A quick wipe keeps the pole sliding smoothly.
A pole that slips under load is a hazard overhead. Inspect locks for wear.
Keep them indoors at partial charge. Cold garages shorten pack life.
Fine debris and bark flakes block the fan. A clear intake keeps airflow up.
Cracks change the air path and lower speed. Replace a damaged nozzle.

faq.q: Can a leaf blower really clean gutters?
faq.a: Yes, for loose, dry or lightly damp leaves. A pole blower with an angled head flushes them out from the ground. It cannot clear packed, rotted muck or a full downspout.
The tool-only ADOTOCAM sits at the lowest tier if you own DeWalt packs. The iToolMax and Feihu sit in the middle, and the Seesii at a higher tier. Spend for reach and battery size.

faq.q: Is a pole blower safe to use?
faq.a: It is safer than a ladder, but wear eye protection because debris flies. Keep the tool away from power lines and do not extend a metal pole near wires. Stand to the side, not under the gutter, and have a helper watch for passers-by so the debris cloud does not hit them. Never use a pole blower on a wet, windy day when the pole can swing.

A pole of about 8 to 9 feet clears a single-story gutter from the ground. A two-story gutter needs a longer adjustable pole and still may need another method. Check eave height first, and remember that the angle of the tube cuts the real reach well below the pole length. A nozzle that has to climb at a steep angle also loses its jet before it reaches the trough, so more pole length does not always mean more cleaning.

faq.q: Do I need high CFM or high MPH?
faq.a: Both help. Volume carries leaves along the trough and speed breaks wet debris loose. A balanced tool like the Seesii does the best job.

faq.q: Will it clear a gutter guard?
faq.a: It will clear leaves off the top of a guard, but it will not clean debris trapped underneath. Blow in the direction of flow and expect to rinse the rest.
